<section class="story-intro">
<p class="eyebrow">Real city data · four-step calculation · observable feedback</p>
<h1>From city activity<br>to <em>road flows.</em></h1>
<p class="lede">See how trips are generated, distributed, split by mode and assigned to roads. Central Boston connects all four stages through a common GMNS network—and shows where transit observations change the calculation.</p>

<div class="step-index" aria-label="The four stages of the saved Boston workflow">
<a href="#stage-1"><span>01</span><b>Trip generation</b><small>How many trips?</small></a>
<a href="#stage-2"><span>02</span><b>Trip distribution</b><small>Where do they go?</small></a>
<a href="#stage-3"><span>03</span><b>Mode choice</b><small>Which way to travel?</small></a>

</div>

<div class="soft"><div class="wrap"><section id="four-step-workflow">
<div class="sectionhead"><h2>Four stages.<br>Actual saved results.</h2><p>The figures below show model outputs, not just map layers. Inputs, calculations and interpretation are linked at every step.</p></div>
<div class="four-step-cards">
<article class="stage-card" id="stage-1"><div class="stage-copy"><p class="eyebrow">01 · Trip Generation</p><h3>Households become trip productions.</h3><p>Area-allocated ACS households × transferred regional rates, with activity-based attraction weights.</p><strong class="result-line">816,054.67 modeled workday person trips</strong></div><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-1-trip-generation"><img src="assets/boston/four_step_results_r1/step1_generation.png" alt="Actual saved zonal production totals grouped by six purpose codes."></a><div class="stage-footer"><p>Regional mean-rate transfer, not an observed local trip count.</p><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-1-trip-generation">Inputs → calculation → productions</a></div></article>
<article class="stage-card" id="stage-2"><div class="stage-copy"><p class="eyebrow">02 · Trip Distribution</p><h3>Productions become OD demand.</h3><p>Gravity/IPF and purpose/time-specific direction conversion distribute trips between H3 zones.</p><strong class="result-line">177 × 177 HBW midday OD matrix</strong></div><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-2-trip-distribution"><img src="assets/boston/four_step_results_r1/step2_distribution.png" alt="Saved modeled HBW midday origin-destination matrix."></a><div class="stage-footer"><p>22,807.22 modeled midday person trips. Not GPS-derived passenger OD.</p><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-2-trip-distribution">Margins → impedance → OD</a></div></article>
<article class="stage-card" id="stage-3"><div class="stage-copy"><p class="eyebrow">03 · Mode Choice</p><h3>Service costs change mode shares.</h3><p>Scheduled and adjusted transit journeys drive a nested response around regional baseline shares.</p><strong class="result-line">4.0990% → 4.2246% walk-access transit</strong></div><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-3-mode-choice"><img src="assets/boston/four_step_results_r1/step3_mode_response.png" alt="Saved percentage-point mode response for panel_od_019 at 12:30."></a><div class="stage-footer"><p>One case, μ_transit = 1. S1 is not an OD-specific absolute-cost baseline.</p><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-3-mode-choice">Itinerary costs → probability → person demand</a></div></article>
<article class="stage-card" id="stage-4"><div class="stage-copy"><p class="eyebrow">04 · Traffic Assignment</p><h3>Vehicle demand becomes road flow.</h3><p>The same static FW solver loads the eligible private/occupied-vehicle panel onto the common network.</p><strong class="result-line">202.078384 → 202.070733 vehicle trips</strong></div><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-4-traffic-assignment"><img src="assets/boston/visual_release_r1/boston_panel_flow_s1.png" alt="Saved S1 modeled panel vehicle flow on Central Boston roads."></a><div class="stage-footer"><p>Fixed panel without regional background traffic—not citywide measured congestion.</p><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-4-traffic-assignment">Vehicle OD → FW → directed-link flow</a></div></article>
</div>
<div class="scope-bridge"><b>One linked workflow; deliberately different scopes.</b><p>Regional generation → HBW demand → 36 selected OD pairs × 3 midday departures → 78 eligible OD–time cases → the vehicle-assignment panel. The full regional total is not loaded to roads. Thirty incomplete cases keep their demand and exclusion records.</p></div>
<div class="actions"><a class="button primary" href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md">Read the complete four-step result →</a><a class="button" href="datasets/boston-four-step-sources.md">Download plot data and provenance →</a></div>
</section></div></div>
<div class="wrap"><section id="gps-feedback" class="gps-story">
<p class="eyebrow">Not just a map of points</p><div class="sectionhead"><h2>What does GPS<br>actually change?</h2><p>It changes a transit service-time input. The dependent journey costs, mode demand and road-flow response are then recomputed—not the regional trip total.</p></div>
<div class="feedback-chain" aria-label="GPS feedback dependency"><div><small>Observe</small><b>Vehicle position<br>and service interval</b></div><span>→</span><div><small>Estimate an input</small><b>Interval-time<br>adjustment</b></div><span>→</span><div><small>Stage 03</small><b>Transit cost<br>and mode response</b></div><span>→</span><div><small>Stage 04</small><b>Vehicle demand<br>and road flows</b></div></div>
<div class="feedback-case"><div><span class="tag">One actual saved trace</span><h3>Route 749 · direction 1</h3><p>Stop pair 1788 → 5093 has <strong>86 s sample-derived elapsed time versus 180 s planned</strong>. Its declared interval adjustment changes the saved result for <code>panel_od_019</code> at 12:30.</p><p class="note">The adjustment is retrospective and exploratory. All 13 interval factors are off by default, each supported by one event. It is not an independently validated forecast.</p></div><div class="tablewrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Same OD–departure</th><th>S1</th><th>S2</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Transit time</td><td>29.052 min</td><td>27.486 min</td></tr><tr><td>Fare</td><td>$1.70</td><td>$1.70</td></tr><tr><td>Walk-access transit</td><td>4.0990%</td><td>4.2246%</td></tr><tr><td>Vehicle trips</td><td>2.164631</td><td>2.161796</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<div class="visual-grid"><figure class="figure-tile"><a href="datasets/boston-central.md#one-saved-transit-position-projection"><img src="assets/boston/visual_release_r1/boston_gps_projection.png" alt="A separate recorded segment illustrates GPS positions projected onto matched road reference lines."></a><figcaption><b>First, establish the spatial link.</b>The original projection map uses a different recorded segment. It illustrates road matching, not the exact event in the numeric trace above.</figcaption></figure><figure class="figure-tile"><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-4-traffic-assignment"><img src="assets/boston/visual_release_r1/boston_panel_flow_delta.png" alt="Saved aggregate S2 minus S1 fixed-panel flow differences; maximum absolute change about 0.006603 vehicle trips."></a><figcaption><b>Then, inspect the model response.</b>78 links differ; maximum |Δ| ≈ 0.006603 panel vehicle trips. Link totals combine multiple OD cases, not just the one illustrated trace.</figcaption></figure></div>
<p class="focus-note"><strong>Switch it off and verify the connection.</strong> Srestore independently disables the overlay and recomputes service costs, probabilities and demand, returning the comparable results to S1. This verifies a computational dependency, not empirical accuracy. GPS does not estimate the regional total, gravity β or all passenger OD in this example.</p>

</section></div>

<div class="soft"><div class="wrap"><section id="gmns-foundation"><div class="sectionhead"><h2>GMNS foundation and toolchain alignment</h2><p>Open the same Boston roads, H3 zones, hierarchy and zonal vehicle demand as a versioned exchange, then trace their links to the saved four-stage and GPS results.</p></div><p>177 fine-zone centroids retain separate identities even when they share one of 139 physical access nodes. The pinned GMNS Plus structural reader opened both S1 and S2 exports; a reversible adapter recovered the original physical solver inputs. The connector arcs are nonphysical and have no invented routing costs. This is format and relationship evidence, not new model calibration or teacher approval.</p><div class="actions"><a class="button primary" href="datasets/boston-gmns-exchange.md">Open the GMNS data contract →</a><a class="button" href="../examples/boston/gmns_exchange_r1/README.md">Files and runnable commands →</a></div></section></div></div>
